title: operator-immersive-poc-day-outline-and-runner-notes
content:
Goal: Run a one-day immersive operator POC with the customer platform/infra team to validate private/dedicated deployment flows, verify model fallbacks and observability hooks, and capture runbook gaps. This doc is the day-of outline + facilitator "runner" journal (notes to self), assumptions, and checklist.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: Customer infra/platform engineers (operators), Redwood SE lead, Redwood SRE/infra engineer (dedicated/private SME), 1 product manager (observer).
- Scope: provisioning, config drift, simple traffic cutover, SLA/latency smoke tests, failure injection, and runbook handoff. Not: long-term cost modeling (we'll surface results later).

Prework required (send to customer 3 days prior):
- Provide 2 sample request workloads (jsonl) and 3 representative prompt templates.
- Grant test VPC peering + ephemeral VPN creds (expires 48h after POC).
- Share a list of internal endpoints and any firewall rules.
- Confirm test accounts for their observability stack (Datadog/NewRelic/Prometheus).
- Confirm 1 operator point-of-contact and preferred Slack channel.

Room / infra checklist (ops):
- Laptop with SSH and gcloud/aws cli preinstalled (SE machines), USB-C to ethernet dongle.
- Dedicated test GPU node(s) available and accessible via ephemeral auth.
- Docker image tags for the model service: redwood/model-serving:v2.3-opsdemo.
- Sample keys: test-KMS-key (rotated), test service account with least privilege.
- Console access: Redwood Console demo tenant + ability to create rollout policy.

Run-of-show (9:00–17:00) — timeboxed blocks with intent and facilitator cues:
- 09:00–09:15 — Welcome + objectives (Priya)
  - Quick round of intros (name, role, 1 expectation)
  - Readout of success criteria: deploy in test VPC, validate fallback, observe latency <250ms p50 for 512 tokens, run canary traffic and rollback.
  - Housekeeping: breaks, Slack channel, incident playbook link.

- 09:15–10:00 — Environment walk and access validation (Ethan)
  - Verify VPN, SSH, and test account auth.
  - Confirm GPU node health, container runtime, and image pull.
  - Facilitator note: if auth fails, escalate to customer network lead — planned contingency: use shared demo node (ENG-1429).

- 10:00–11:15 — Baseline deploy: model service + KV cache soak (Sofia)
  - Steps: pull image, start service, attach model shards, warm KV cache with provided prompts.
  - Slide/outlines: 'Deploy steps', 'Common failure modes and fixes' (see slide skeleton).
  - Exercise: run 100 synthetic requests; capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost estimate.
  - Runner note: save curl commands in /tmp/poc-commands.txt; capture logs at /var/log/redwood-demo.log.

- 11:15–11:30 — Standup: early results and blockers
  - 3 quick datapoints: success/fail of deploy, baseline latency, one action item.

- 11:30–12:30 — Canary traffic and rollout policy (Priya + SE)
  - Configure a canary that sends 10% traffic to new deployment for 15 minutes.
  - Show Redwood Console rollout view and metric thresholds.
  - Exercise: trigger canary, watch metrics and tracing waterfall.
  - Facilitator cue: if error rate >2% for 5m, demonstrate auto-rollback.

- 12:30–13:15 — Lunch (informal Q&A with PM)

- 13:15–14:15 — Failure injection lab: network and OOM scenarios (Ravi)
  - Simulate high latency to model shard, simulate GPU OOM (kill process), and ICA (intermittent connection).
  - Observe telemetry, fallback to compatible model family, and cache warming after restart.
  - Exercise: trigger fallback and verify functional parity on 10 representative prompts.
  - Runner note: note exact commands used for simulation and save as 'failure-sim.sh'.

- 14:15–15:00 — Observability deep-dive + custom dashboards (SRE)
  - Walkthrough: token-level cost traces, per-route latencies, and KV cache hit rates.
  - Quick dashboard build: p50/p95 latency by route, error rate, model variant used.
  - Exercise: add an alert rule for sudden increase in p95 by 30% within 5m.

- 15:00–15:30 — Breakouts: operator runbook drafting (three teams)
  - Each small group drafts a 6-step runbook for a specific incident: (A) model shard crash, (B) sustained high tail latency, (C) failed rollout.
  - Deliverable: 1 page runbook snippet + required access list.
  - Facilitator note: circulate template runbook and encourage explicit rollback commands.

- 15:30–16:15 — Runbook readout + alignment (all)
  - 10–12 minute readouts from each group, collect to confluence stub.
  - SEs to fill open actions and owners.

- 16:15–16:45 — Acceptance tests and success measurement (PM)
  - Agree on pass/fail criteria for POC (latency, cost band, successful rollback, onboarding docs).
  - Capture a one-week follow-up plan for perf soak.

- 16:45–17:00 — Wrap & next steps (Priya)
  - Immediate deliverables: combined runbook + sprint tickets + demo recording.
  - Ask for feedback via short pulse survey link.

Slide skeleton (speaker notes in parentheses):
- Slide 1: Title + Objectives (1 slide)
  - Bullet: Day goals, attendees, success criteria
- Slide 2: Architecture snapshot (diagram) (call out model variants, KV cache)
- Slide 3: Deployment run steps (short checklist)
- Slide 4: Rollout policy and metrics to watch (p50/p95, error rate, cache hit)
- Slide 5: Failure injection scenarios and expected behavior (fallback paths)
- Slide 6: Observability tour (screenshots of dashboards + traces)
- Slide 7: Runbook template + incident owner table
- Slide 8: Acceptance criteria and follow-up plan

Facilitator-runner tips (notes to self):
- Keep demos timeboxed: two minutes to spin up the image demo, five minutes for the canary watch.
- When a blocker happens, verbalize the impact and the rollback plan immediately.
- Use the phrase: "observable-first troubleshooting" to nudge customers toward metrics-driven ops.
- Save all generated logs/artifacts to the shared drive folder with timestamped names.

Artifacts to produce by EOD:
- Combined runbook (single-page + links to commands).
- Short demo recording (10–12 min highlights).
- Ticket backlog: ops follow-ups + infra changes + SSO/keys rotation.
- Post-POC note to customer summarizing findings and recommended next steps.

Acceptance criteria (template for negotiation with customer):
- Deploy in their test VPC and handle 500 RPS synthetic burst for 2 minutes without exceeding 2% errors.
- P50 latency <250ms for 512-token prompts, P95 <750ms.
- Successful auto-rollback during injected failure within 3 minutes.
- >70% KV cache hit on warm runs.

Risks and mitigations (short list):
- Network access delays: mitigation — pre-validated VPN + fallback to shared demo node.
- Missing observability hooks: mitigation — instrument short-term sidecars to emit the minimal traces.
- Customer policy/approval time: mitigation — run key steps using demo tenant and separate acceptance window.

Parking lot / open questions (to resolve during pre-call):
- Do they have HSM/KMS policies that block our test keys? (owner: customer security)
- Are there egress limits on their test VPC? (owner: customer infra)
- Which model variants are acceptable for fallback from their regulatory standpoint? (legal review)

Post-POC follow-ups (timeline):
- 24h: share recording + runbook draft.
- 72h: Redwood SE to open follow-up tickets and provide recommended quantization/pricing tradeoffs.
- 1 week: perf soak results and proposal for Dedicated capacity sizing.

Notes to self (casual):
- Keep the theory short; let them run the keyboard. Operators love control knobs.
- Bring spare ethernet dongles.
- If canary fails due to rate-limiter, show how to tune batching and token limits as quick wins.

Attachments/cheat commands (save to artifacts folder during run):
- quick-deploy.sh — pulls image, writes env, and launches service
- canary-fire.sh — synthetic traffic generator (100 RPS)
- failure-sim.sh — network delay and process kill routines

References:
- Confluence: SE operator POC runbook (CONFLUENCE:SE-operator-poc-runbook-9281)
- Jira: ENG-1429 (shared demo node fallback)

End of doc.
